Posterior probability of a safety signal under the EXP_BERN model

Source: R/expbern_post.R
expbern_post.Rd

Computes the posterior distribution of the rate ratio under the exponential Bernoulli (EXP_BERN) mixture model of Duncan (2026), which models whether each subject had the event during the individual follow-up time and does not assume a Poisson distribution for the number of subjects with the event.

Usage

expbern_post(
  y,
  t,
  k = 1,
  lambda_hp,
  pt_hp,
  df = 1,
  p_prior = c(0.5, 0.5),
  rr0 = 1,
  cutoff = 0.95,
  t_star = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  details = TRUE,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

y

Vector of event indicators (1 if the subject had at least one occurrence of the event during follow-up, 0 otherwise).

t

Vector of follow-up times (positive), in the same time unit as lambda_hp, pt_hp and t_star.

k

Randomization ratio of study drug to placebo (k:1).

lambda_hp

Event rate in the historical placebo population.

pt_hp

Total patient time at risk in the historical placebo population, or Inf for a known background rate lambda_hp.

df

Discount factor for the historical data (df >= 1 discounts the historical information).

p_prior

Shape parameters c(a, b) of the Beta prior for \(p\). The default c(0.5, 0.5) is the prior used by Duncan (2026).

rr0

Critical value of the rate ratio (\(\theta_c\) in Duncan, 2026).

cutoff

Posterior probability threshold for a signal.

t_star

Optional time at which the cumulative incidences are summarized.

level

Probability of the equal-tailed credible interval of the rate ratio.

details

Logical; if FALSE, the quantiles of \(r\) are not computed (faster; used in sim_oc).

control

List of settings for the numerical integration: n_coarse (cells per coordinate of the coarse grid, default 41), n_lambda (Gauss-Legendre nodes, default 48), n_p (Chebyshev points, default 49), check (default TRUE), eps (default 1e-8) and max_iter (default 12).

Value

An object of class bssd_post; see bdribs_post. The element model is "EXP_BERN", estimates contains the posterior means of \(p\), \(r\), \(\lambda_p\) and \(r \lambda_p\) (lambda_d), and integration contains the nodes used and the error estimate.

Details

For subject \(i\) with follow-up time \(t_i\), the model is $$P(Y_i = 1) = w_p [1 - \exp(-\lambda_p t_i)] + w_d [1 - \exp(-r \lambda_p t_i)],$$ with \(w_p = 1 / (k + 1)\) and \(w_d = k / (k + 1)\), and $$\lambda_p \sim \mathrm{Gamma}(\lambda_{HP} PT_{HP} / DF, PT_{HP} / DF), \quad r = p / [k (1 - p)], \quad p \sim \mathrm{Beta}(a, b).$$ The Gamma distribution is parameterized by shape and rate.

The two-dimensional posterior is integrated numerically on the coordinates \(\log \lambda_p\) and the prior distribution function of \(p\). The latter keeps the tails of the posterior of \(p\) under control: the likelihood does not vanish as \(r \to 0\) or \(r \to \infty\), so these tails follow the prior. A coarse grid first locates the region that holds all but control$eps of the posterior mass in each marginal. On that region, Gauss-Legendre quadrature is used for \(\log \lambda_p\), and the marginal density of the second coordinate is interpolated at Chebyshev points, which gives its distribution function at any point (used for prob and the quantiles of \(r\)). When control$check is TRUE, the computation is repeated with about 1.5 times as many nodes, the finer result is returned, and the absolute difference in prob is reported as the integration error estimate.

Because the likelihood stays positive as \(r \to \infty\), the posterior means of \(r\) and \(r \lambda_p\) are infinite when the second shape parameter of the Beta prior is 1 or less, as for the default c(0.5, 0.5). They are then returned as Inf, and the posterior median of \(r\) is the summary to use.

A signal is declared when \(P(r > rr_0 \mid \mathrm{data}) > \) cutoff.

References

Duncan, B. (2026). Robust safety monitoring and signal detection using alternatives to the standard Poisson distribution. Journal of Biopharmaceutical Statistics, 36(2), 227–244. doi:10.1080/10543406.2024.2395532

See also

bdribs_post, llbern_post

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 100
t <- runif(n, 10, 52)
y <- rbinom(n, 1, 1 - exp(-0.004 * t))
fit <- expbern_post(y, t, k = 1, lambda_hp = 0.003, pt_hp = 2000, df = 2,
                    t_star = 52)
fit
#> Model: EXP_BERN 
#> Relative risk: rate ratio r of study drug to placebo
#> P(r > 1 | data) = 0.6589
#> Signal (posterior probability > 0.95): no
#> Posterior of r: mean Inf, median 1.573, 95% interval (0.02978, 10.1)
#> Cumulative incidence at t_star = 52: placebo 0.1739, study drug 0.2425, difference 0.06865
